diagnosis.headline: The payment container has stopped (exited with code 137, not OOM-killed, at 05:33:12Z), so every checkout PaymentService/Charge call fails with DNS or no-route errors. Checkout is at a 75% error rate and order emails have stopped.

root_causes.cause: The payment container stopped at 05:33:12Z with exit code 137 (SIGKILL, not OOM-killed) and has not restarted (restart_count 0). Its DNS name no longer resolves and its old IP 172.21.0.16 has no route, so every checkout Charge call fails and checkout returns errors upstream.

affected_services.impact: Container exited, so no payment can be charged
PlaceOrder fails because PaymentService/Charge cannot reach payment (DNS lookup error / no route to host); error rate 0.75
Checkout requests return errors to users (frontend error rate 0.0308)
Errors from failed checkouts are passed through to users (error rate 0.0196)
No order-confirmation emails go out because orders fail before the email step (silent, no warn/error logs)

ruled_out.reason: The checkout container is healthy and its calls to cart, shipping, currency and product-catalog succeed. Its only failures are client calls to payment.
The email container is healthy with no warn/error logs. It is silent only because orders fail at the payment step before email is called.
No errors (error_rate 0.0), container healthy. The traffic drop follows overall load, not a fault.
Request rate is flat over 30m, so there is no flood.

open_questions: What sent SIGKILL to payment at 05:33:12Z, given oom_killed is false? A past dry-run restart of payment at 04:09 suggests this has happened before.
Frontend memory is at 94.59% of its 250 MB limit and rising over the last hour (E24). It is not causing errors now but could lead to an OOM kill. Check it for a leak.

Recommendation/frontend rps are well below baseline, but load-generator and frontend-proxy rates were steady or rising over 30m (E21, E22). This is probably a different load level from the baseline period, not a fault. Confirm.
prevention: Set a Docker Compose restart policy (restart: unless-stopped/on-failure) on payment so a killed container comes back automatically
Alert directly on payment container state and health (exited/unhealthy), not only on downstream checkout errors
Find out what sent SIGKILL (exit 137 with oom_killed=false), e.g. a manual docker stop/kill or the host, and control who can stop containers
Add retry/circuit breaking and clear user-facing errors in checkout for payment outages

proposed_action.reason: The root cause is a stopped container (exit 137). Restarting payment restores the Charge endpoint that checkout depends on.
proposed_action.risk_assessment: Low risk: payment is down already, so a restart only brings it back. If something external sent the kill (exit 137 without OOM), it may stop again. Watch the container state after the restart.
proposed_action.expected_outcome: payment returns to running/healthy, its server spans come back (about 0.057 rps), checkout error rate drops from 0.75 to about 0, and email traffic resumes as orders complete.
